mem.10:
Andrew started a Financial Analyst job the week of March 20, 2023. He has no pets but loves animals; birds awe him, especially strong, graceful eagles. He has spotted birds while hiking, not gone bird-watching. Fox Hollow is a favorite weekend trail with great views.

Audrey has dogs Pepper, Precious and Panda (she’d had them for three years as of March 27, 2023); she recently got them collars and tags. They explore parks and trails with her. On April 2, she said her household had adopted Pixie, a small white puppy (photo: Pixie on a carpet). Pixie took days to adjust to the other dogs but now plays and explores with them; Pepper and Pixie are especially close. Caring for Pixie delayed Audrey’s visit to a previously discussed hiking spot. Audrey said she had four dogs on May 11 and again on July 3; on June 13 and 26 she referred to her two dogs. On July 3, she said all four were 3-year-old mutts: two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes. Preserve these differing counts/references. The dogs are a close pack; they love running and playing fetch. Photos on July 3 showed two dogs running in a field with a ball, two curled up in a dog bed, and two on a couch under a blanket. They had a lively, fun doggy playdate on Friday, June 30.

Andrew was considering adopting a dog but struggled to find a dog-friendly city apartment. Audrey recommended housing websites with dog-friendly filters. Andrew hoped to find both a place and a dog; he missed hiking with his family dog (shared photos of the dog on a couch and people hiking with dogs) and said dog hikes build bonds and memories. By May 6 he was browsing websites, visiting shelters, and asking friends; a small dog seemed best for an apartment, and he advised considering space and breed exercise needs. He contacted landlords and checked neighborhoods, hoping for a home near a park or woods. He had not adopted yet and planned another shelter visit. As of June 2 he still had not found suitable housing, felt somewhat discouraged but determined; Audrey offered to help and asked him to email his criteria. Andrew mentioned a nearby doggy daycare with a large indoor play space. He said he would visit Audrey’s recommended dog park and report back. On July 3, he still couldn’t find dog-friendly rentals and called it a bummer; he described life as throwing curveballs.

Andrew feels connected, at home in his soul, and restored by nature when life is chaotic; city life makes getting outside difficult. He seeks greenery, mountain views and fresh air, finds nature peaceful, invigorating and therapeutic, and tries to hike outside the city at least weekly. He takes photos to share nature’s peace and inspire others. He often turns to nature for a mental reset. On the weekend of April 8–9, he and his girlfriend tried a city café to explore and unwind; they had croissants, muffins, tarts and coffee (photo). Audrey made blueberry muffins during April 9–15 and proposed a future pastry party with Andrew; he agreed and she said her dogs would come. No date/place set.

Audrey finds dog walks and nature grounding, joyful and meaningful. Her arm tattoo of a dog and sunflowers represents love for her dogs and nature; she got it before April 16 so she could see their happy faces when apart. She walks dogs in parks, lets them explore at their pace (usually about an hour), and says walks are their favorite part of the day. They enjoy hikes, scents and outdoors; she prioritizes safety with leashes and shoes. She plays fetch with balls/frisbees and arranges park playdates. Her energetic dogs enjoy meeting other dogs and get excited at toys; they tolerate party hats for treats. She recommended a dog park beside her usual walking park, with trees and benches. On April 16 she shared photos of dogs running and a woman walking dogs in woods. On a hike the week of April 24–30, she saw a hummingbird with wings spread. On May 5, she road-tripped with her dogs to a national park; she takes them on such trips about every couple months. On a hike there sometime May 26–June 1, she reached a peak and enjoyed sunset, breeze and birdsong. A June 2 favorite photo showed two horses in a fenced field; she said nature cheers her and makes her grateful. She also shared photos of dogs playing in a field/meadow on June 13. On July 3, she said nature is calming and restorative with her dogs around and shared the running-dogs field photo.

On May 11 Audrey said she had four dogs and spent much free time keeping them happy and healthy. She signed up for a June positive-reinforcement pet-bonding workshop after finding its flyer at a pet store, where a volunteer introduced her to a friendly, playful dog. She expected her quick-learning, reward-loving dogs to do well and promised Andrew tips and updates. She believes punishment is wrong and does not want to hurt her dogs. Andrew said he’d look into such classes. Audrey shared a photo of dogs with a yellow circle; Andrew called one adorable. By July 3, she was taking a dog-training course that was challenging but rewarding, taking a lot of time, and her dogs were already doing better. She was pleased with their progress and said they give her love and happiness.

Andrew found a new nearby hiking open space by May 3; on the weekend of May 6–7 he hiked with friends and girlfriend at a recently found spot. He shared a dirt-path-to-grassy-hill photo. On June 11 he took a beginner rock-climbing class with friends, reached the top with their encouragement, and found it challenging, satisfying and fantastic. He felt proud and shared climbing and summit-view photos. On June 13 he said it inspired him to try kayaking and possibly bungee jumping; nature pushes him beyond his comfort zone.

During the week before June 13, Audrey found a small park with a tree-lined trail and invited Andrew to walk with her dogs; he accepted. She calls being outdoors with dogs her happy place. On June 1 she watched them run and play off leash at a park, which brought peace and joy. On June 26 she said she’d moved into a new house with a bigger backyard; her two dogs enjoyed running and exploring, and she’d set up an agility/play area with toys. She was still unpacking. Andrew hiked with friends in good weather on June 23 and took photos he had not yet reviewed by June 26. Years earlier, Audrey hiked with friends to a mountain lake, where they sat, talked and admired the peaceful scenery; she remembered it as calming. By July 3 Audrey hadn’t had much time for new trails due to dog training; Andrew said he was missing trail peace and making do with urban adventures.

On July 3, Andrew said he’d been finding new hobbies while unable to hike, including cooking and trying recipes. Cooking helps him de-stress, be creative and relax; he called himself a rookie but enjoyed experimenting and likes the reward of eating what he makes. Audrey loves cooking, experimenting with recipes, and sees it as an escape, self-care and therapeutic. She likes putting on music, pouring a glass of wine and going with the flow in the kitchen. Her favorite recipe is chicken pot pie, especially cozy on a cold day; it’s a longstanding family recipe that reminds her of her grandmother’s kitchen and conversations at the table. She offered to send Andrew the recipe and said she’d do so “in a bit”; actual delivery not confirmed. Photos showed a pie on a wooden board with a knife and a lattice-top pie. Her go-to ingredient is garlic, for its smell and taste. She offered to send Andrew her roasted chicken recipe too; it’s based on her love of Mediterranean flavors and uses chicken, garlic, lemon and herbs. She called it an easy, healthy favorite comfort meal. Photos showed a vegetable-rich plated dish and a pan of chicken and potatoes on a stove. Andrew appreciated the recipes, planned to try them and promised to report back; no result yet.
mem.19:
Andrew began a Financial Analyst job the week of March 20, 2023. He loves animals, especially birds and eagles, and spots birds while hiking. He recommends Fox Hollow for views. Nature makes him feel connected, restored, peaceful, and at home; city life makes access difficult. He tries to hike on weekends, enjoys greenery, mountains, and fresh air, and takes photos to share nature’s calming effects.

Audrey has four dogs: Pepper, Pixie, Precious, and Panda. By July 3, 2023, she described them as two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes, all three years old. Their personalities differ: the oldest is relaxed, the second playful, the third sometimes naughty but cuddly, and the youngest lively and adventurous. She calls them her most important companions and says they bring her joy, peace, meaning, love, and happiness. They like fetch, frisbees, trails, new scents, playdates, and exploring; Audrey uses leashes and shoes for safety. She walks them about an hour at their pace and says walks are their favorite part of the day. She also plays fetch, arranges dog-park playdates, and puts party hats on them for treats. Her nearby dog park has trees and benches. By June 26 she had moved to a home with a larger backyard and agility equipment/play area. Their favorite resting spots: Pepper—the couch; Pixie—the bed; Precious—the chair; Panda—the rug; they also cuddle together. By September 24 she said her dogs mostly play with one another, not other furry pals.

Audrey uses positive-reinforcement training and opposes punishment. She enrolled in a workshop for June 2023 and later took a challenging training course; by August 4 she was attending agility classes twice a week. She teaches obedience and tricks such as sit, stay, shake, and roll over, and says training is fun and rewarding. She recommends patience, regular training, time, love, and praise to build trust. She learned grooming in a course and recommends gentle, patient grooming, especially around ears and paws, plus daily brushing, baths, and nail trims. On August 16 she took all four dogs to the vet; it was chaotic, so she planned to take them one at a time. She might like more dogs someday, but four keep her busy. She makes personalized wooden name tags for pets. Her tattoos include a dog and sunflowers (love of dogs/nature), and later all four dogs. Her childhood dog Max loved fetch; she remembers long neighborhood walks and confiding in him. She sometimes road-trips with her dogs (about every couple of months); on May 5, 2023, they visited a national park. She once hiked to a peak there for sunset, breeze, and birds (May 26–June 1). She enjoys nature as refuge and restoration, likes lakes, and recalled a peaceful mountain-lake visit with friends. She has never fished.

Andrew initially considered adopting a dog but struggled to find dog-friendly housing. He searched websites and shelters, asked friends, contacted landlords, and wanted a home near parks/woods; he thought a small dog best for apartment living. Audrey offered to help find housing if he emailed his criteria. Andrew brought home Toby on July 11, 2023; by August 4 he described Toby as a young male German Shepherd, smart and loyal. Andrew wanted to bond with him and hike when feasible; Audrey advised that puppy care takes time, attention, walks, and activity. Andrew hoped to learn care himself and have outdoor adventures with Toby. In September, he still had not found dog-friendly housing, and Toby was too young for hikes.

Andrew and Audrey planned a hike with Audrey’s dogs and Toby for August 2023, but never confirmed a date or place. They wanted a safe trail where the dogs could run freely. Andrew and his girlfriend enjoy finding cafés and restaurants; on the weekend of April 8–9 they tried a café with croissants, muffins, and tarts. They picnicked July 7. Andrew volunteered with his girlfriend at an animal shelter July 24; Audrey had never volunteered but hoped to someday. Andrew planned camping with his girlfriend and Toby (Aug 4), visited a farm for vegetables (Aug 16), and went fishing with her Aug 19–20. He took a rock-climbing class June 11, reached the top with friends’ support, and liked the view; afterward he considered kayaking and possibly bungee jumping. He hikes with friends, including May 6–7 and June 23, and planned a nature-reserve visit Aug 19–20. Hiking calms and invigorates him; reaching a summit makes worries vanish.

Audrey bakes blueberry muffins and suggested a pastry party with Andrew in April; it remained a future plan with no date or location. She loves cooking as creative self-care, often with music and wine. Favorite: family chicken pot pie, which reminds her of her grandmother. She also loves garlic and Mediterranean-inspired roasted chicken with lemon and herbs. She offered recipes; Andrew said he would try them July 3. Andrew is a beginner cook who experiments to de-stress. By July 3 work and housing difficulties had led him to cook more and seek hobbies. Work stress curtailed outdoor time in July and September. On Sept 6 he said morning coffee and lunchtime walks helped him recharge; Audrey aims for one self-care activity daily. Audrey’s neighbors’ dogs had a playdate with hers by Sept 6. Andrew hiked over the Sept 2–3 weekend and photographed a sunset over the city. Earlier shared photos included dogs, trails, a mountain sunset with a church, horses, and Audrey’s dogs playing.

**Session 19 — September 24, 2023:** Andrew and Audrey resumed chatting after a long gap. Audrey said that the previous Friday, September 22, one of her dogs saw something at the park and pulled so hard that the leash broke. She feared the dog might run off or get hurt, chased and caught her safely, then calmed her with petting, hugs, a calm voice, and a slow walk. She said incidents like this remind her how important the dogs are and strengthen their bond. She shared a photo of a red retractable leash with black handle. Andrew sympathized and said he felt anxious imagining Toby getting lost; he referred to the dog as Precious, but Audrey had not specified which dog it was. He asked how to build a strong bond with Toby. Audrey advised patience, regular training, giving dogs time and love, and praising success. Andrew agreed dogs may need different amounts of time to bond.

They discussed Audrey’s dogs’ training, walks, breeds, and affection for them. Audrey said she walks them multiple times daily for exercise and bonding; all are mutts—two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes. Andrew shared a photo of flowers on his balcony and said caring for them was something he had been doing lately. Audrey said she has a small garden, with flowers and a growing vegetable patch, and finds watching plants grow relaxing, peaceful, and satisfying. Andrew asked about the flowers; Audrey identified them as Peruvian lilies, describing their bright colors and delicate petals. They are easy to care for, needing watering and enough sun. Audrey said the dogs enjoy running around and exploring the garden. The conversation ended with both emphasizing how much their dogs mean to them.
mem.28:
Andrew and Audrey, Mar–Nov 2023

- Mar 27: Andrew had started a Financial Analyst job the week of Mar 20. No pets yet; loved animals, especially eagles, and noticed birds while hiking. Recommended Fox Hollow for hikes/views. Audrey had dogs Pepper, Precious, and Panda, then about three years old; they explored parks and trails.
- Apr 2: Audrey’s household adopted white puppy Pixie; she settled in over days and bonded especially with Pepper. Audrey was too busy with puppy care to visit a hiking spot. Andrew wanted a dog but struggled to find pet-friendly housing; Audrey recommended rental sites with pet filters. They shared dog photos.
- Nature was a recurring theme: Andrew found greenery, mountains, fresh air, and trails restorative, but work/city life limited time outdoors. He hiked weekends when possible and took nature photos. Audrey found dog walks and nature calming; her dogs liked exploring, fetch/frisbee, parks, and hikes. She emphasized leashes, shoes, safety, and playdates.
- Apr 8–9: Andrew and girlfriend tried a city café and shared pastry/coffee photo. Audrey shared blueberry muffins and suggested a future pastry party with Andrew and dogs; no plans fixed. Audrey had a dog-and-sunflowers tattoo for her love of dogs/nature. Apr 24–30 she saw a hummingbird on a hike.
- May 3 Andrew found nearby hiking open space. May 5 Audrey road-tripped with dogs to a national park (she takes them away every couple months). May 6 Andrew sought a small dog and dog-friendly apartment near parks/woods, visiting shelters/asking friends; still dogless. He hiked with girlfriend and friends. May 11 Audrey said she had four dogs and signed up for June positive-reinforcement training; she opposed punishment. Her dogs learned quickly and liked rewards.
- Late May/early June Audrey hiked with dogs to a national-park peak, enjoying sunset, breeze, birds, and gratitude. Jun 2 shared photo of two horses in fenced field. She offered housing-search help if Andrew emailed criteria. Jun 11 Andrew took beginner rock-climbing class with friends, reached top, felt proud; wanted kayaking, possibly bungee jumping. Audrey invited him on a tree-lined dog walk; he accepted (her walks ~1 hour, dogs set pace). Jun 26 Audrey moved to house with bigger backyard/dog agility area; Andrew mentioned indoor doggy daycare nearby. She recalled a calming mountain-lake hike.
- By Jul 3 Audrey’s four 3-year-old mixed dogs: Pepper and Panda are Labrador mixes; Precious and Pixie Chihuahua mixes. (Earlier described as two Jack Russell and two Chihuahua mixes.) They got along and played fetch. Audrey’s challenging training course limited trail time. Andrew still had housing trouble, cooked to relax. Audrey loved cooking; offered family chicken pot pie (reminded her of grandmother) and Mediterranean roasted chicken (chicken, garlic, lemon, herbs; garlic her go-to). Andrew wanted both. Jul 7 Andrew picnicked with girlfriend.
- Andrew/Audrey planned an August dog hike, trail safety to be checked. Jul 11 Andrew got male German Shepherd puppy Toby (photo); work stress kept him indoors. He invited Audrey and dogs to hike in August; she accepted, no date/place set. Audrey made engraved wooden pet tags. Jul 24 Andrew and girlfriend volunteered at shelter; Audrey hoped to volunteer someday and later donated jewelry profits to a shelter. Audrey’s childhood dog Max loved fetch/walks; she confided in him. Jul 27 dog personalities: oldest relaxed, second playful, third naughty/cuddly, youngest lively/adventurous.
- Aug 4 Andrew planned camping with girlfriend and Toby; hoped Toby would hike with him. Audrey did agility twice weekly, recently took dogs on 2-hour scenic hike; advised puppy German Shepherd needs time, walks, attention. Aug 16 Audrey got tattoo of all four dogs; vet visits with all at once were chaotic. Pepper couch, Pixie bed, Precious chair, Panda rug; cuddle/best friends. Four enough for now, though maybe more someday. Toby liked fluffy floor blanket. Audrey took grooming lessons; advised gentle, patient grooming, especially ears/paws. Aug 19–20 Andrew/girlfriend fished at nearby lake; Audrey hadn’t fished but liked lakes. She stressed brushing, bathing, nail trims, affection; Andrew hoped to bond with Toby.
- Sep 6 Andrew said work stress curtailed outdoors; coffee and lunchtime walks helped. Audrey did daily self-care and arranged neighbor-dog playdate; dogs got new beds late Aug/early Sep. Andrew hiked at sunset Sep 2–3; Toby too young for hikes. Sep 22 Audrey had leash break at park but caught/soothed dog. Used patience, praise, training; taught sit/stay/shake/roll over and walked dogs several times daily. Garden flowers/vegetables; Sep 24 identified Peruvian lilies, needing sun/water.
- Oct 1 Andrew/girlfriend planned November beach trip with Toby and discussed November dog hike with Audrey. Audrey walked dogs at grassy shaded park Sep 30; dogs swam at beach that weekend. She wanted to try birdwatching; accepted Andrew’s offer (pending schedule); he’d bring binoculars/notebook and teach local birds. They discussed ecosystems, recycling, transit/biking; he offered river bike routes. Oct 4 Andrew missed nature, considered houseplants; Audrey offered advice. She made recycled-material jewelry, donated some profits to shelter. Oct 10 Andrew/girlfriend/Toby played board games; Oct 13 another game night and planned café. Audrey’s dogs liked socializing/fetch/frisbee, disliked snow; Toby chased squirrel. Oct 16 Audrey bought toys; later injured arm at park and wore cast, complicating dog care.
- By Oct 19 Andrew adopted shelter dog Buddy; Toby and Buddy needed adjustment. He enjoyed walks with Buddy and planned hikes with both. Audrey/Andrew planned Nov 4 hike; Audrey would research site and bring snacks. Oct 21–22 Andrew/girlfriend wine-tasted. Oct 24 Andrew tried sushi for first time; Audrey recommended California/salmon rolls and planned sushi dinner. Oct 25 Audrey took dogs to behaviorist for unusual behavior; used routine changes/positive reinforcement, gradual progress; hoped to hike again. Discussed unnamed dog-friendly scenic lake trail and autumn-color hike.
- Nov 4 Andrew and girlfriend biked to a park outside city; he had Toby and Buddy (rest of message incomplete).
- Nov 17 (Friday before Nov 22): Audrey took dogs to pet salon; they were excited, then settled and behaved well. Shared grooming photo (one dog on table with leash), shiny coats.
- By Nov 22 Andrew and girlfriend had adopted another dog, Scout, shortly before; photo showed a woman feeding a dog hay in a barn. Name chosen for adventurous spirit. Planned first outing with Scout, Toby, Buddy to nearby small park; keeping Scout leashed and gradually introducing them. Bought bed, toys, puppy pads to make safe/comfortable space. Audrey advised small gradual outings, leash safety, slow introductions. Audrey shared photo of a dog running with tennis ball. Dogs on both sides described as beloved family, bringing joy and friendship; Audrey’s dogs were doing well, exploring and meeting people.
